en: The *Brahmaṇa-mṛtyu-parihāra-sūtra* Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Anxi śramaṇa An Shigao of the Later Han Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the Anāthapiṇḍada Park.
In the Grove.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"In the past, there were four brahmin seers who diligently cultivated the five supernormal powers of the wholesome dharma and were constantly fearful of death."
At that time, four brahmin seers, who had diligently cultivated the five supernormal powers through wholesome dharmas, thought to themselves:
"In what place should we dwell so as to remain in the world forever?"

At that time, there was a certain brāhmaṇa who had diligently cultivated wholesome dharmas and possessed great supernormal power and the five superknowledges; he then entered into mid-air, [thinking]: "Within this, there is no death."
The one who had entered emptiness then passed away.

A second brahmin, having diligently cultivated the wholesome dharmas and attained the five supernormal powers, feared death and entered the great ocean, thinking: "In the midst of the ocean, there shall be no death for me."
He then passed away in the midst of the ocean.

The third brahmin, who had diligently cultivated wholesome dharmas and possessed great power and the five supernormal faculties, entered the interior of a mountain out of fear of death, and there he met his end.

That fourth brahmin, having diligently cultivated the five supernormal powers of wholesome dharmas and possessing great majestic power, feared death and entered the earth, thinking: "I shall escape death there."
Thereupon, they passed away on the spot.

At that time, the World-Honored One, with his pure and stainless divine eye, observed those four brahmins as they diligently cultivated wholesome dharmas; possessing great majesty and the five supernormal powers, yet fearing death, one passed away while suspended in mid-air, another passed away having entered the sea, another passed away having entered the belly of a mountain, and another passed away having entered the earth.

At that time, the World-Honored One, seeing that those four brahmins were diligently cultivating wholesome dharmas and possessed the five supernormal powers with great majesty, spoke these verses: "Not in the sky,
nor in the midst of the sea, Nor by entering into mountain clefts—
There is no place on earth Where one may escape and not undergo death."
At that time, the bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Brāhmaṇa Avoiding Death Spoken by the Buddha.
